extracted.intended_audience: actors, theatre students, dramatic critics, and general readers interested in the craft of acting
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for judging or producing powerful stage acting and the professional conduct that supports it, as exemplified in 19th-century theatrical biography. Focuses on voice, presence, interpretation, study, and moral/professional habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature-as-revelation (not artifice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acting should be 'no effort of will, no trick or art of calculation, but nature itself uncovered and set free' — performance as revelation rather than simulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page contrasts mere simulation or calculated tricks with an acting that seems to come from 'the centres of his nervous system' and is 'inspired intuitions, infallibly true and irresistibly sensational.' Example: Kean's effects described as nature 'set free' and sometimes on the verge of madness. Anti-pattern: affected, obviously staged mannerisms or deliberate artifice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possession by character
rubrics_metrics.description: The actor penetrates and incorporates himself with the character until 'they possessed him,' so the performance is not imitation but embodiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard praises actors who seem inhabited by their roles (Kean), producing performances that feel inevitable and internally motivated rather than externally assumed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of passion to audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The true actor can 'transmit his thoughts and passions into others' so the audience's imaginations and feelings react in accord with the actor's ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as the one test of the true actor: if the actor's ideal moves the audience to react emotionally, defects are pardoned; if not, merits are ineffectual. Example: Forrest's capacity to carry the sympathies of the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unitary, elemental intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: Great effects arise from 'unitary and elemental' impulses that strike 'the automatic centres' and produce overwhelming, awe-filled reactions in sensitive auditors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acting that evokes a primal or archetypal response (compared to 'flashes of lightning') is prized. Performances should aim for concentrated, elemental impact rather than diluted or diffuse expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocal expressiveness and timbre
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice must convey a wide emotional palette — resonant, tense vibrations in fury; husky whispered horror in suggestion; mournful melody that 'sank into the soul.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Kean's stammering staccato for frenzy; husky slide on 'nor secure' in Forrest's Iago; Othello's farewell described as an anthem/dirge. Guidance implies careful control of pitch, tone, tastefully timed emphasis, and the ability to make voice an instrument of atmosphere and feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climacteric delivery and control of climaxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver climactic points ('climacteric points') with almost undiminished power, producing shocks like 'striking lightning' even amidst weariness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The actor should reserve and shape energy to make pivotal moments explode convincingly. Example: Forrest's fourth-act outburst that electrified the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and psychologically plausible readings
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret roles with original, convincing conceptions that reveal plausible human motives (e.g., Forrest's reading of Iago as outwardly gay and jovial while secretly malicious).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original choices that deepen character (not merely novel for novelty's sake) are praised and can become the new standard ('everybody who speaks the part hereafter must do it just so'). Anti-pattern: stale, obvious caricatures (the 'sullen and sombre villain' Iago).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtlety of expressive detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Small vocal or physical inflections (a husky tone, a whispered word) that betray inner knowledge or feeling are powerful tools for affecting audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use controlled, sudden breaches of surface demeanor to let the character's interiority shine (example: Forrest's husky 'nor secure'). These micro-moments can produce dramatic reactions and influence future interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity, variety, and vigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Acting ought to be 'sincere, so varied and vigorous' — exhibiting honesty of feeling, dynamic range, and energetic commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid monotony or false display; combine truthful emotion with physical and expressive variation to maintain audience engagement across a performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and avoidance of unmeaning rant
rubrics_metrics.description: Conception and delivery should be clear and unpretentious — 'clear and correct in his utterance, graceful in his action, he never offends us by unmeaning rant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize intelligibility and purposeful gesture over bombastic, empty declamation. Example: contemporary praise contrasted Forrest favorably with rants that lack meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-possession and deliberate technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibit calm control and deliberate intention — 'remarkable self-possession and deliberate way of doing just what he intended to do' — to strengthen stage effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplined carriage and purposeful choices reassure audiences and managers; they support consistent performances even when nervous. Anti-pattern: visible trepidation or purposeless rushes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stagecraft: attitudes, gesture, costume, and bearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical aspects — attitudes, gesture, costume, reposeful bearing — significantly contribute to impression and should be carefully managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text notes that careful costume and superb form made a strong sensation; visual tableau and movement amplify vocal and emotional work. Study of pictorial art and costume history is recommended to inform stage posture and groupings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study and cultivation of taste
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustained intellectual cultivation — reading widely in biography, poetry, philosophy, science, studying plastic and pictorial art and costume history — deepens dramatic art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The actor should be a student: reflect on readings, note notable attitudes in art, and use broader cultural knowledge to inform interpretation and realism. This is framed as crucial long-term nourishment of the artist's faculties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical training and bodily development
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain superb bodily condition (exercise, boxing lessons) to support dramatic power: 'basis of a gigantic complacency' and a ground for great stage presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical training (e.g., boxing) builds poise, courage, and a commanding form that audiences admire; the body's harmony underpins highest spiritual power in performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral and professional conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal honor ('my word is as strong as any written contract'), generosity, and restraint from self-destructive habits (gambling, excessive stimulants) are part of the actor's professional standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Forrest refusing to break a verbal commitment despite higher pay; his denunciation of gaming and quitting it after a moral stand. Guidance: personal integrity and avoidance of vices preserve the actor's career and faculties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding human nature for character conception
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceive characters from 'the independent light of what he knew of human nature' — study people and natural human motives to craft believable performances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than relying on stock villainy or fashionable mannerisms, base character work on observations of real human behavior; this yields more subtle, effective portrayals (e.g., Forrest's Iago).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of expression (by-play and realism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use by-play and 'exquisitely artistic realism' — small touches and the play of realistic detail — to set off principal effects and enrich the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Layer performances with realistic small actions and interactions that make big moments more believable (example: voice 'set off with a by-play of exquisitely artistic realism'). Avoid flat, theatrical surfaces with no honest detail.
